failure_summary.description: The context contained the clue verbatim from a J!-Archive-style page ('clue | tongue. right: Leah.'), but the agent skipped it and answered 'liver' from its own guess. It also gave no reasoning before answering.
The agent gave the full name 'Chester A. Arthur' when the clue already supplied the first name ('named Chester'). The gold answer was the surname only, 'Arthur'.

patch.reasoning: Trajectory 1 failed because the agent did not do the verbatim-clue lookup that Rule 3 already describes. The edit spells out the archive layout ('clue | answer. right: Name.'), tells the agent to scan for it before using its own knowledge, and requires quoting the matched line. Trajectory 2 failed on exact-match formatting for a person's name. The current person-name guidance is vague, so the edit says to drop any part of the name already in the clue and to default to the surname when there is no verbatim answer in the context.

edits.target: - Context passages often reproduce the clue text from a trivia/Jeopardy archive (e.g. J! Archive, flashcard sites), followed by the answer (e.g. 'CLUE | answer', after a comma at the end, or in flashcard text). If you find this, copy that answer exactly, in the same form and spelling.
edits.content:
- ALWAYS scan the context first for the clue's distinctive words before using your own knowledge. Passages often reproduce the clue text from a trivia/Jeopardy archive (e.g. J! Archive, jeopardy question dumps on GitHub, flashcard sites), followed by the answer. Typical layouts: 'CLUE text | answer. right: ContestantName.' (the answer is the text between '|' and '. right:'/'wrong:'), 'CLUE, answer', or flashcard 'front / back'. The clue in the archive may be slightly garbled (missing accents or letters, parentheses, dropped words), so match on the distinctive words.
- If you find such a match, copy that answer exactly, in the same form and spelling. It OVERRIDES any guess from your own knowledge or from other passages. Before the answer tags, briefly quote the matched line.

edits.target: For people, prefer the form used in a verbatim answer from the context (Rule 3); otherwise use the name form most natural for the clue.
edits.content: For people, prefer the form used in a verbatim answer from the context (Rule 3). Otherwise give the surname alone, as a trivia answer key usually does ('Arthur', not 'Chester A. Arthur'). Never repeat a first name, title or other name part that the clue already gives (e.g. 'the only President named Chester' -> 'Arthur'). Use the full name only when the surname alone would be ambiguous or the clue asks for a first name.
